newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma grand jury probes bombing cover-up.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma grand jury probes bombing cover-up.

text.p: A state grand jury was selected Monday to begin a fresh investigation into claims that federal agents knew the Oklahoma City bombing was coming and that not all the killers have been caught.
The 12-member panel drawn from a pool of 100 Oklahoma County residents was to determine the length and direction of the probe.

State officials had tried to block the probe and doubt it will unearth new evidence on the 1995 blast, which killed 168 people, but they were forced to impanel a grand jury after 10,600 local residents signed a petition demanding it.

Glenn Wilburn, who lost two grandsons in the blast, and Republican state legislator Charles Key led the drive for an independent probe, which they believe will show convicted bomber Timothy McVeigh and alleged co-conspirator Terry Nichols did not act alone.

"I think the grand jury will find there were other people with McVeigh in Oklahoma City who carried out the bombing," said Key, who regularly gives talks on the alleged conspiracy to anti-government groups around the country.

Key hopes the grand jury will hear testimony from several witnesses who claim they saw at least one person with McVeigh before or immediately after a huge truck bomb blew apart the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995.

Police initially released a sketch of a suspect they called John Doe No. 2 but he was never found and prosecutors then said the evidence showed McVeigh planted the bomb and that only Nichols had helped him plan the attack.
McVeigh was found guilty and sentenced to death by a federal jury in a Denver courtroom earlier this month. Nichols is to go on trial Sept. 29.

But Key said he wants the grand jury to look at allegations that some federal agents knew there was a plot to bomb the federal building and either did nothing or botched their efforts to stop it. He also insists more people were involved.

"We want to know what happened to John Doe No. 2 and we want to know about the prior knowledge that some in the federal government had that this attack was going to take place," Key said in a recent interview.
Oklahoma Gov. Frank Keating and other state officials have said they doubt the grand jury investigation can uncover anything missed in a $50 million federal investigation.
